title: Nominativ i akuzativ
titleEn: Subject and the thing you want
theme: Želim kahvu shows who does the wanting versus the thing you want.
reviewerNotes: Bosnian editor pass. Accusative forms check out (kahvu, kuću, most, pivo, Emira, želim/želi). Fixed garbled pattern opener, englishLies phrasing, and theme wording that mixed accusative with dative ('gets it'). Still draft pending human publish decision. Residual native spot-check after Fact Checker mold repairs (2026-09-09T14:53:05Z): re-checked cases, conjugations, glosses, Latin/diacritics, and quiz/try keys; focus on Ch9 Popijem present-as-future, Ch5 vocatives, Ch13 shelf balance, and Ch11 trebati (recommend only, no silent rewrite).

whyHere.heading: Why you are here
whyHere.body: Today you learn why Ana says Želim kahvu instead of Želim kahva. The list word names the coffee. The moved ending marks the coffee as the thing she wants. English keeps coffee still in both jobs. Bosnian dresses the word again. You already filed the piles in Chapter 1. This chapter is only the name-it job versus the want-it job.

englishLies.heading: Why English lies
englishLies.body: English lies because the phrases this is coffee and I want coffee use the same letters. You already do a tiny Bosnian trick with people when you say I if you do the thing and me if the thing happens to you. Coffee in English never bothers. Bosnian coffee does. The list form kahva is the name-it job. Kahvu is the same she-word in the want-it job. Schools call those jobs nominativ and akuzativ. You can keep saying name-it and want-it and still be right.

knownLine.heading: A line you already say
knownLine.body: Book 1 already gave you Ana’s line Želim kahvu, which means I want coffee. Chapter 1 told you to ignore the moved letter for one day. Today that letter is the whole point. Kahva is the list form that names the drink. Kahvu is the want-it form on the same she-word. The pile did not flip to he. The job in the sentence changed.
knownLine.speaker: Ana

pattern.heading: The pattern
pattern.body: She-pile words swap that final a for u when they are the thing you want. Kahva becomes kahvu, and kuća becomes kuću, because those words already sit in the she pile from Chapter 1. He-pile things usually keep the list form in that same job, so most stays most when you want the bridge. Leftover-pile words usually keep the list form too, so pivo stays pivo when you want the beer. People who do the wanting stay in the name-it form. Ana želi kahvu keeps Ana still while coffee moves. Learn the she move first. Then notice that most and pivo often look unchanged.

howYouGuess.heading: The pests
howYouGuess.body: Two pests will trip you today, and both are worth memorizing early. The first pest is saying Želim kahva, which leaves coffee in the name-it form when Ana wants it. The second pest is he-pile people. Emir stays Emir when you name him, but he often becomes Emira when you see him or want him, because people in the he pile take an a in the want-it job. A bridge does not. Do not argue with Emira. Just remember people and things follow different habits in this job.

trick.heading: The bit that tricks you
trick.body: The trap is to hear kahvu and decide coffee switched piles to he. It did not. The u is a job mark on the same she-word you filed yesterday. The other trap is to force every word to move like kahva. Most and pivo often stay still in the want-it job, and that stillness is still correct. If you rewrite most into a fake she ending, you invent a word nobody said.

nerd.heading: Why it's like this
nerd.body:
Old English is the English of England about a thousand years ago, not a class you missed. Farmers and priests around Winchester hung extra letters on thing-words to show the job in the sentence. You still own a scrap of that habit when you say I if you do the thing and me if the thing happens to you. He and him work the same way. Coffee lost those outfits in later English. You speak the later version.

Bosnian never fired the outfits on kahva. The name-it form and the want-it form are leftover job marks, the same family of work as I and me. Schools call the whole family case. Today you only need two jobs from that family. Tomorrow’s job is the of and none form on the same coffee.

items.prompt: Amira names the coffee. Which form?
items.explanation: This is the name-it job, so you use the list form.

items.prompt: Ana wants a house. Which form?
Emir wants a bridge. Which form?
items.explanation: He-pile things usually keep the list form in the want-it job.
Leftover-pile words usually stay still here.
He-pile people often take a in the want-it job. Emira is the pest.

items.prompt: Someone says Želim kahva. What went wrong?
options: They left coffee in the name-it form.
items.explanation: Wanting needs kahvu. Kahva is the list form for naming it.

items.prompt: Kahvu still belongs to which pile?
items.explanation: The u is a job mark. The pile stayed she.

items.prompt: In Ana želi kahvu, which word moved for the want-it job?
items.explanation: The person doing the wanting stays in the name-it form. Coffee moves.

items.prompt: Why does most often look the same when you want it?
options: Because he-pile things often keep the list form in this job
items.explanation: She-words move. Many he things and leftover words stay still. Emira is the people pest.

questions.question: What is today’s system?
options: Name-it versus want-it on the same word
Filing he, she, and leftover piles
questions.explanation: Piles were Chapter 1. Today is only the name-it job versus the want-it job.

questions.question: Želim kahvu uses which form of coffee?
options: Want-it form on the same she-word
questions.explanation: Kahva became kahvu because Ana wants it. The pile stayed she.

questions.question: She-pile words like kahva and kuća usually do what in the want-it job?
questions.explanation: Kahvu and kuću. That u is the job mark, not a new pile.

questions.question: Why is Želim most often correct without changing the bridge?
options: Most is leftover like pivo, so it must become mostu
He-pile things often keep the list form in this job
questions.explanation: Most stays most. Pivo often stays pivo too. Emir is the people pest.

questions.question: Vidim Emira. Why not Emir?
options: He-pile people often take a in the want-it job
Emir switched to the she pile
questions.explanation: People and things diverge here. A bridge stays most. Emir often becomes Emira.

questions.question: What comes next after name-it and want-it?
options: The of and none job on the same coffee
questions.explanation: Chapter 3 is genitive. Nema kahve is the preview. Still no mega-chart.

next.body: You now know why Želim kahvu is not Želim kahva, and why most and pivo often look unchanged in that same job. Emira was the people pest. Chapter 3 is the of and none job on the same coffee, the line Nema kahve. You still will not get a seven-job chart.
